question.text: LP Ms. Ananya Singh has committed INR 10 crore to 'Godavari Cat III AIF'. The Manager issues a drawdown notice of 30% with a 10-business-day payment window. Ms. Singh fails to remit on the due date. Under typical AIF agreements, what is the MOST likely immediate consequence for Ms. Singh?

answer.text: Interest accrues on the delayed payment, and continued default may lead to loss of rights/returns, reduction of commitment, or in extreme cases termination and return of capital invested
Her full commitment is automatically forfeited and returned to the sponsor
The Manager is personally liable to the fund for her shortfall
The fund must be wound up automatically

explanation.text: The Logic: Drawdown notices typically state the payment date along with consequences for default. The source-stated consequences include interest for delayed payment, reduction of commitment, loss of rights or returns, and in extreme cases termination and return of capital invested. The Trap: Option B is too extreme — automatic forfeiture of the full commitment is not the standard mechanism. Option C wrongly shifts liability to the Manager. Option D fabricates an automatic wind-up consequence. Note: The specific default consequences applicable to an LP are those set out in the fund's contribution agreement and drawdown notice.
